title: Methodus generalior numeros quosvis satis grandes perscrutandi utrum sint primi necne?

deep.reconstruction:
Context: E719 turns Euler's theory of numeri idonei (convenient or idoneal numbers) into a practical primality test. On the previous page he gave the table of idoneal values of the product αβ, with the property that a number represented in only one way by αx²+βy² is prime. This page (§§35-40) states the general Problem: given a large N, decide whether it is prime.

§36: Write N = αa² + βb² with αβ idoneal. Euler advises taking α and β as large as possible, since this shortens the later search (compare the 3x²+199y² example for 1000003 on the previous page).

§37: N is composite if and only if it has a second representation N = αx² + βy². If one is found, the factors follow from the earlier rules. If none exists, N is prime.

§38: Equating the two representations gives αa² − β(y² − b²) = αx². It is better to take α as the larger coefficient. Then α must divide y² − b². Euler requires gcd(α,β)=1, gcd(x,β)=1 and gcd(y,α)=1.

§39: If α is prime, α divides y+b or y−b, so there is a single case. If α is composite, its factors may be split between y+b and y−b. Each splitting into two factors must be examined separately: one extra case if α has two factors, more if it has more.

§40: For each splitting α = μν (with μ or ν allowed to be 1), set y+b = μp and y−b = νq. Then y² − b² = αpq. Dividing by α leaves the reduced equation a² − βpq = x².

The next page eliminates y (2b = μp − νq), parametrises p and q linearly in s using the convergent condition mν − nμ = 1, and searches for squares by subtracting second-order differences from a². In modern terms this is a finite search for representations, organised by the residue classes of y modulo the factors of α.
errors: Euler concludes that N must be prime if no second representation exists. Even with the coprimality conditions, a unique primitive representation by an idoneal form can also occur for certain prime powers and small multiples of primes. Example: 25 = 3²+4² is its only primitive representation by x²+y². This caveat to Euler's idoneal criterion was later made precise (Grube, Gauss's genus theory). The page omits the hypotheses that N is coprime to 2αβ and is not such a prime power.
§39 says a prime α gives 'unicus tantum casus'. Strictly, α|y+b and α|y−b are two cases. They are symmetric under y → −y, so this is harmless.
The splitting α = μν with y+b = μp, y−b = νq tacitly assumes μ and ν are coprime. This is only stated later (§45). Even α, or repeated prime factors, need extra care, since gcd(y+b, y−b) divides 2b.

ideas.what: A number uniquely (primitively) represented by αx²+βy² with αβ idoneal is prime; used as a primality test.
ideas.modern_name: Euler's idoneal number criterion; class group of exponent ≤2 (one class per genus)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E708, E719, E725 and others; letters to Lagrange and Fuss), with corrections by Gauss and Grube
ideas.where_published: E708, E719, E725; Nova Acta Petropolitana; discussed in Dickson's History, Vol. I, and Weil's Number Theory

ideas.what: Reducing the second-representation search to α | y²−b², split over factorizations α = μν, giving a² − βpq = x².
ideas.modern_name: Search for representations by binary quadratic forms via congruence conditions on y modulo α (sieve-like, akin to Fermat-style difference-of-squares searches)
ideas.where_published: E719 itself (this page); related computations in E699/E708

ideas.what: Choosing large α, β (large idoneal αβ) to shorten the search.
ideas.modern_name: Heuristic choice of discriminant to minimise search range

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard, well-documented part of Euler's idoneal-number primality method (E719 is discussed in Dickson and Weil). The page is a routine algebraic set-up with no novel results; the prime-power caveat is a known historical correction.
transcription_corrections: §40: 'ita ut fit yy − bb = αpq' should read 'ita ut sit'.

The scan is a four-page spread. The pages labelled 34/35 at the left and bottom, with columns 6561, 2040, 4521, −1020, 7561 and 'Hic jam occurrit numerus quadratus ...561 = 19²? ... y = 19, s = −5', belong to adjacent pages of the volume, not to page 24/25 of E719.
